Oḍayadeva
also known by his title vAdIbhasiMha. Dig. Jain writer, pupil of Puṣpasena an. probably also of Somadevasūri, an. fellow-pupil of Vādirāja (a. of Yaśodharacarita). See Śrutasāgara's C. on Yaśastilakacampū

. His Gadya- [Page095-a. cintāmaṇi (p. 4, Intro., Tanjore edn., adya dharA nirAdhArA nirAlambA sarasvatI, reminiscent of the popular verse on the death of King Bhoja of Dhārā ‘adya dhArAº’), suggests for him a date later than Bhoja (A.
-1053). Vādībhasiṁha is a. epithet used by several scholars. Hultzsch,

. p.. 697-8, suggests his identity with Oḍayadeva Śrī Vijayadeva of Śravaṇabelgola, pupil of Kanakasena Vādirājadeva. T. S. Kuppuswami Sastri (Intro. to his edn. of Gadyacintāmaṇi) tries to identify Oḍayadeva with Ajitasena of Malliṣeṇapraśasti on the basis of the title Vādībhasiṁha.
See N. Premi, Jain Sāh. aur Itihās, p.. 477-82.
--Kṣattracūḍāmaṇi. padyakāvya, in 11 cantos on Jīvandhara. On its similarity with the Tamil work Jīvakacintāmaṇi of Tiruttakkadeva, see notes to the edn. by T. S. Kuppuswami Sastri, Sarasvatī Vilāsa Series 3, Tanjore, 1903.
--Gadyacintāmaṇi. gadyakāvya, in 11 lambakas on the legendary hero Jīvandhara, based on Guṇabhadra's Uttarapurāṇa.
Ed. by T. S. Kuppuswami Sastri an. S. Subrahmanya Sastri, Sarasvatī Vilāsa Series 1, Tanjore, 1902.

Oḍāśaṅkara
See Śaṅkara, son of Sudhākara an. grandson of Śucikara.
